newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish investment abroad rises 30 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Spanish investment abroad rises 30 pct in 1996.

text.p: Spanish direct investment abroad grew 30 percent in 1996, the Spanish commerce and tourism ministry said in a statement on Sunday.
Spanish investment abroad was a total 1.2 trillion pesetas ($8.4 billion) compared with 948 billion a year earlier, the statement said.
The ministry cautioned however that 200 billion pesetas of these funds were related to restructurings in the financial-services sector and stemmed from previous years.
But because they were accounted for in 1996, they represent an over-estimation in investment abroad last year.
Excluding these activities, Spanish investment abroad rose nine percent in 1996 compared with 1995.
More than half of this figure, or 56.8 percent, stemmed from acquisitions, compared with just 32 percent a year earlier.
Latin America was the most important destination for these funds, absorbing 40.5 percent of the total. Within this region, Argentina, Chile, Venezuela and Brazil were the most important destinations.

The Spanish financial sector led the internationalisation process, spending 31.5 percent of last year's foreign investment total. This sector also gained prominenece among investments, with 27.6 percent of the funds invested spent on the financial sector.
